## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cūḷabodhicariya* (Cp 14, also numbered as II.4) is a verse narrative in the *Cariyāpiṭaka* illustrating the Bodhisatta's perfection of moral conduct (*sīla*) [SuttaCentral; Appleton 2010]. In this account, the Bodhisatta permits his wife to be abducted against her will, maintaining that he would not break his *sīla* even if an attacker were to harm her with a knife [Appleton 2010]. Richard Morris observes that this story resembles the *Buddhabodhijātaka* [Morris 1882]. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Sujato under the title *The Conduct of Cūḷabodhi* [SuttaCentral].

Pali-internal text reuse identified by DharmaNexus shows seven shared passages between the *Cūḷabodhicariya* and the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā*, notably across verses 4.4–5.4 [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated alignments, DharmaNexus detects matches with Tibetan translations, including the *Damamūko-nāma-sūtra* (D0341) and the Mahāyāna sutra *thabs mkhas pa chen po sangs rgyas drin lan bsab pa'i mdo* (D0353) [DharmaNexus].
